newsitem.title: CUBA: Castro calls meeting with pope a "miracle".
newsitem.headline: Castro calls meeting with pope a "miracle".

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro said on Tuesday his meeting with Pope John Paul II at the Vatican was a "miracle" and thanked the Vatican for opposing the longstanding U.S. embargo of the communist-ruled nation.
Castro, speaking at a lunch with senior Vatican officials in remarks broadcast on Cuban state television, said: "For me it is a miracle that I have been able to greet the pope."
In Rome, chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said the pope had accepted an invitation from Castro to visit Cuba and the trip would take place next year.
Castro, 70, who was educated by Jesuits, was full of praise for the pontiff. He said that as a child he could hardly have imagined meeting the pope.
The Cuban leader said he was grateful he had been received in so "friendly" a fashion. The meeting had left him with "an unforgettable impression," he said.

Castro, who has been in power in Cuba since 1959, described himself as a "modest fighter and a modest politician" who did not deserve such an honour and added he was impressed by "the greatness and humility" of the pontiff.
Speaking to Vatican dignataries, he added he was grateful for Vatican support against the 34-year U.S. embargo on Havana. The Vatican has several times condemned the embargo.

Cuban television, which along with Vatican television was the only media allowed access to the meeting between Castro and the pope, showed images of the pope handing Castro a white Bible during their meeting.
Castro's first words to the 76-year-old pontiff were that he hoped that the pope, who underwent surgery recently to remove his appendix, was in good health.
